profile.facility_type_note: JFK12 and JFK13 are two of the most historically significant carrier hotel buildings in the world. JFK12 is at 60 Hudson Street, Manhattan, built in 1930 as the Western Union Building, now one of the most important internet peering and interconnection points on the US East Coast. JFK13 is at 32 Avenue of the Americas, built in 1932 as AT&T's Long Distance headquarters, also a major carrier hotel. Both addresses confirmed via Digital Realty's own site.

reading.body:
JFK12 is a carrier hotel at 60 Hudson Street in Manhattan, built in 1930 as the Western Union Building and now operated by Digital Realty as a major internet peering and interconnection point on the US East Coast. The operator does not publish a critical IT power capacity figure for this building, valuing it primarily for interconnection density rather than raw megawattage. No tier-1 source has confirmed individual critical IT megawatts for this facility in this research pass.

This campus does not drive AI scaling through power supply. Carrier hotels are transit and peering infrastructure, not compute platforms. The absence of published power specifications reflects the building's function: it hosts the network equipment and cross-connects that route traffic between providers and cloud platforms, not the accelerator racks and GPUs that run AI workloads.

Among 31 mapped data center facilities in New York State, only one publishes megawatt capacity, totaling 3 MW. JFK12 ranks second by published megawatts in the state, a reflection of how little critical IT power capacity is disclosed anywhere in New York. The state's data center footprint is opaque.
